title: Anyone signed in can open anyone's account page
explanation: getAccount checks that someone is signed in, but never that the account is theirs: Ada can read Linus's email by changing the id. The PR says anyone else gets 403. Add the same check updateEmail has: if (account.id !== request.user.id) return { status: 403 }.

title: The account page sends passwordHash to the browser
explanation: The whole user object goes into the response, passwordHash included, which breaks the rule that it never leaves the server. Build the body from the fields the page needs: { ...publicProfile(account), email: account.email }, as updateEmail does.

title: The new email is saved without checking it
explanation: Whatever arrives in the body is stored: an empty string, "hello", or no email at all. The PR promises 400 for anything that doesn't look like name@domain; check it before saving.

title: No test tries someone else's account, or a bad email
explanation: The getAccount tests only use the owner and a signed-out user, so the missing 403 slips through, and no test sends a malformed email. Add both cases: they would have caught the two bugs above.
